name: The keeper of Ashfold
descriptor: a rawboned keeper in a stained apron
notes: The target of `silence-the-keeper`, which D-526 calls the low-cast workhorse. He stands at the tavern DOOR, not behind a bar: every tile of Ashfold's tavern footprint fails canStandAt, and the threshold is better anyway because D-549 put the square where every route crosses. WARNING: the descriptor is a MATCH KEY -- the round engine decides the objective with an exact comparison against it (D-593), so rewording it to read better makes the objective unwinnable. validate:content refuses that. ashfold-townsfolk is a townsman rather than a publican and is the honest placeholder: he is the only authored human not in a helmet, and a keeper of his own is one file in the studio. ⚠ HIT POINTS (D-619): 40, where every NPC silently had the world's spawn default of ten -- a number set for test fixtures that no content file could ever reach. The arithmetic, measured rather than guessed: a level-1 character with the arming sword its kit grants swings at +3 against an unarmoured AC of 10, so it hits about seven times in ten for a flat 3, which is 2.1 a swing; a basic character gets ONE swing per four-second combat round (D-550). Ten hit points was therefore five swings and twenty seconds, and the stakeholder's note is that the objective is 'over in seconds if the player directly attacks the keeper'. Forty is about nineteen swings and seventy seconds of standing over somebody in the open square where D-549 put every route -- long enough for the watch to close (D-619 makes it run) and for anybody crossing to see it. That is the fight this objective is supposed to be about. It halves for two attackers, which is D-529's buddy system doing its job rather than a leak. UNRATIFIED, and the first number to move if a minute of swinging reads as a chore rather than as a scene.
